Default-off privileged native 2.0.1 Set/Clear commands preserve exact native EVSE, transaction and schedule identity, purposes, recurrence, validity and decimal rates including zero. Admission and durable ownership prevent unsafe dispatch; exact generation-scoped phase proof gates phase selection. An independent persistent software peer observes same-ID replacement, nested AND criteria, protected external constraints and unchanged state on denial; delayed, duplicate, disconnected and restarted commands do not replay automatically.

Privileged, explicitly opted-in OCPP 2.0.1 GetCompositeSchedule queries (K08) require Accepted registration, a live exact-resource capability and either the grid connection (station scope, evseId 0) or the exact advertised EVSE, a positive duration and an optional W/A unit; denied, extended or out-of-scope requests send no CALL. Accepted replies retain the schedule for the requested EVSE within the requested horizon and forced unit, with ordered periods, exact tenths including zero and native phase fields; Rejected keeps typed status and a standardized case-insensitive reason. Malformed or inconsistent CALLRESULTs are uncertain without fabricated evidence and CALLERROR is a sanitized rejection. Evidence survives stale writers and restart; delayed replies permit heartbeat progress, duplicates are one-shot and reconnect never replays. No local calculation, snapshot change or physical effect is inferred.

Privileged, explicitly opted-in OCPP 2.0.1 GetChargingProfiles queries (K09) carry either profile IDs or other criteria (K09.FR.03) and a scope-bounded evseId; a signed native requestId stays retired per connection. The native Accepted/NoProfiles acknowledgement is durably recorded before the command outcome is released; after Accepted, ReportChargingProfiles fragments are routed by the socket owner, acknowledged with an empty response, sanitized against the exact query (EVSE, sources, criteria) and collected in arrival order within the shared multipart bounds until the final non-tbc fragment. Profiles keep EVSE, limit source, purpose including external constraints, kind, validity and one to three schedules with exact tenths; customData is dropped and salesTariff is omitted and flagged. Out-of-query fragments, malformed fragments, disconnect, limits and restart end the report as incomplete without partial inventory; terminal reports are frozen and nothing is replayed. Reported profiles never become local policy or physical evidence.

Charger-reported external charging limits (K11-K14) are answered with an empty response only after the source, grid criticality and exact schedules are durably committed as latest-state points on the grid connection (absent evseId) or an exact configured EVSE, plus one bounded typed journal record that omits but counts schedules beyond the evidence bound. CSO-sourced limits, zero or unconfigured EVSEs and malformed schedules are refused with a CALLERROR and change nothing (K11.FR.05, K12.FR.04). ClearedChargingLimit marks only the matching source and scope inactive (K13.FR.02, K14.FR.03). Repeated limits create no command, no observed command effect and no CALL, and the state survives restart. The bridge does not calculate or enforce any limit.

Charging needs (K15/K17) are answered only after the exact AC or DC needs, the linked transaction and the bridge's answer are committed. The bridge computes no schedule and never answers Accepted: Rejected with NotEnabled by default, Processing only for an operator-asserted EMS on a station with a canonical or native profile path, and Rejected with UnknownEvse or TxNotFound without a configured EVSE or exactly one current transaction; mismatched or missing parameter sets are a CALLERROR (K15.FR.06). EV charging schedules (K15-K17) are checked against the TxProfiles this bridge installed for that transaction, rebuilt from retained requests: Accepted when none exists or every interval is within the highest-stack limit, Rejected with ValueTooHigh when any interval exceeds it, and Rejected with Unspecified when the limits cannot be placed exactly. The bridge sends no profile and starts no renegotiation on its own. No ISO 15118 or certification claim.
